findings.title: Exit code 4 silently changes meaning (recreate -> feature disabled)
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. The exit code is the documented, scriptable contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` (see docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc). Any existing automation or operator logic that treats exit code 4 as "recreate upgrade required" will now interpret a "feature disabled" outcome as a recreate request, and will treat the new recreate code 3 as an unknown failure. If the code numbering must change, consider keeping 4 as recreate and using a new free code (e.g. 5) for the disabled-feature case, or at least call this break out explicitly in the release/upgrade notes.

findings.title: Feature-disabled path only covered for `metadata`, exit code not asserted
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only runs `update-compatibility metadata` without the feature and asserts the console message. The newly introduced exit code `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (4) is never asserted, and the `check` subcommand's disabled-feature path (the one consumers script against) is not covered at all. Since the whole point of the new code is scriptability, a regression in the returned exit code (or in the `check` guard) would go unnoticed.

findings.title: `rolling-updates` feature is not enabled for the default (null) update strategy cases
findings.body: `createInitialDeployment` returns early when `updateStrategy == null`, so the `ROLLING_UPDATES` feature is only added to the CR for the `RECREATE` parameterization. Both parameterized tests (`testImageChange(null)`, `testCacheMaxCount(null)`) therefore exercise the update logic with the preview feature disabled, while the new documentation states the Operator will fail when `rolling-updates` is not enabled. Either the default-strategy cases should also enable the feature (so they match the documented supported configuration), or the asymmetry deserves an explicit comment/assertion that the legacy path intentionally works without the feature.

findings.title: setEnabledFeatures overwrites any pre-existing enabled features in the test CR
findings.body: The code guards against a null `FeatureSpec` but then calls `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES))` unconditionally, replacing whatever list was already present in the deployment produced by `getTestKeycloakDeployment(true)`. If the base test CR ever enables another feature, it will be silently dropped here and the test will run against a different server configuration than intended (and could mismatch the build-time features baked into the custom image). Appending to the existing list would be safer.

findings.title: Exit code 4 description is wrong for the `metadata` command
findings.body: The exit-code table describes 4 as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled." but the same code is also returned by `update-compatibility metadata` (see UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run), where nothing about an upgrade was evaluated and no metadata was written. The wording should say the command aborted because the `rolling-updates` feature is disabled, so users don't misread a failed metadata generation as a compatibility verdict.
